newsitem.title: UK: William Cook challenges Triplex Lloyd.
newsitem.headline: William Cook challenges Triplex Lloyd.

text.p: William Cook challenged bidder Triplex Lloyd to make a profit forecast for the year ending March 31, 1997 after Britain's competition authorities cleared the engineering group's takeover attempt.
Andrew Cook, chairman of William Cook said Triplex Lloyd "should come clean about its own prospects."
He urged shareholders to ask "William Cook has already made a profit forecast. When will Triplex Lloyd be doing the same?"
Triplex launched its bid in November based on seven of its own shares and 1350 pence in cash for every nine William Cook shares.
A spokeswoman for Triplex said the company did not plan to make a trading statement, given that its half-year results were published on November 11.
William Cook called on Triplex to make a profit forecast for 1997 against the "background of negative reports on the UK and European automotive components market."
Margins in the Triplex division have historically been in decline, having fallen from 8.8 percent in 1992 to 5.8 percent in 1996, said William Cook.

"Clearly William Cook does not understand Triplex Lloyds' business," the spokeswoman said. "Passenger cars account for less than a sixth of Triplex Lloyds' group sales, their automative activities are very much commercial vehicle related with Perkins being the main customer."
